[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Andrew Glasgow was born on 30 December 1775 and baptised on 5 January 1776 at St Cuthbert's, Edinburgh. The parish transcript names his parents as Alexander Glasgow, a brewer's servant, and Agnes Cunningham, and gives the family's residence as Grange.<ref name="FMP">"Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929," Findmypast transcript, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F0734610&tab=this Andrew Glasgow, record SCOT/OPR/BAP/0734610] (accessed 23 October 2026), birth 30 December 1775, baptism 5 January 1776, St Cuthbert's, Edinburgh, Alexander Glasgow and Agnes Cunningham, residence Grange; citing OPR 685_2/9, item 1, p. 275. Original register image not inspected.</ref> The existing profile identifies them as [[Glasgow-1321|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[Cunningham-20926|Agnes Cunninghame]]; the particular adult-profile identification of Alexander remains probable, not proved.<ref name="FMP" /> The [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_691341389&tab=this companion Findmypast index, R_691341389] records the same baptism and parents but uses 1776 as a birth year without a separate birth date.

Possibly the same as [[Glasgow-3165|Andrew Glasgow Esq (abt.1760-1819)]]

=== Distinct 1779 Leith signatory; unproved 1790 merchant identification ===
Andrew Glasgow is a named signatory in a Leith and St Anthony’s journeymen-society notice dated 3 February 1779, under the grouped Preses to annotation.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601805253/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1779-02-09, p.7].</ref>

Andrew Glasgow, merchant in Kirkgate, Leith, is named as a contact where impost warrants may be obtained.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601818940/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1790-12-07, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601819059/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1790-12-10, p.2].</ref>

The grouped annotation "Preses to" does not independently identify Andrew’s society or trade. The Leith name and place make the 1779 and 1790 occurrences compatible, without proving that they concern the same man. Being a contact for warrants does not establish that he held a tax office.

The 1779 signatory cannot be this profile's Andrew: born on 30 December 1775, he was only three when the notice was dated. The 1790 merchant was about fourteen or fifteen if he was this Andrew; the shared name and regional setting alone do not establish that identification, nor does the 1779 notice bridge it. Keep the merchant as an unproved later-life comparison only.<ref name="FMP" />
